correctness.rationale: Finite-branch separated affine similarity dimension is the unique decreasing pressure root. Evaluation at 1/q gives exactly aH_N, so sign and integer crossing follow from H_N. Euler-Maclaurin and the Laurent expansion of the Riemann zeta function yield the exact polynomial cutoff prefactor. Uniform log-pressure Taylor estimates on the bounded critical window and the logarithmically growing crossover window yield the two dimension asymptotics. The second derivative is a weighted variance bounded by the squared maximal log branch index. The verified finite checker corroborates pressure identities but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The first-order published theorem leaves the transition at tau=1/lambda unresolved. At that location the true finite alphabet cutoff differs from the exponential approximation by a diverging polynomial multiplicative factor. Determining it, including its Euler constant, is a natural exact computational-complexity benchmark for finite-alphabet approximation. The uniform second-scale dimension profile and strictly positive log-enhanced boundary displacement quantify what the first-order theorem cannot decide, not an arbitrary finite test.
